findings.title: What it is
findings.said: A contract the explorer calls FiatTokenV2_2.

findings.title: How old the contract is
findings.said: It was created 8 months ago, in block 4035507 (the chain has no code at this address one block earlier).

findings.title: Can anyone read the code
findings.said: The source of the code behind this proxy (0xc35b…eae8) is published and verified on pharosscan.

findings.title: Can its code be swapped
findings.said: Yes, by one private key: it is a proxy running 0xc35b…eae8, and its proxy admin is a plain wallet, 0x46f9…3f1b.
findings.why: Whoever holds that one key can swap the code at any moment, without asking anyone, including for code that drains what you approved.

findings.title: Has its code been swapped
findings.said: No: the same implementation has been in place since the contract was created (block 4035507).

findings.title: Who has approved it
findings.said: Nobody approved it to move their tokens in the last 100000 blocks (about 26 hours).

findings.title: What its owner can do
findings.said: Its bytecode has functions to create new tokens out of nothing (mint); freeze all transfers (pause); block particular addresses from moving their tokens (blacklist).
findings.why: These are normal in many tokens, but each one is a lever someone holds over your money. The source is verified, so you can read who may pull it.

findings.title: Have you dealt with it before
findings.said: Yes: it appears 38 times in your history, the last time 6 hours ago.

findings.title: Does it imitate someone you pay
findings.said: No: none of the 52 addresses you've paid shares its first and last four characters.
